summary: A 1934 Civilian Conservation Corps BC-201 fireman-lookout cabin in the Shasta-Trinity National Forest, now rented by the Forest Service through Recreation.gov.

facts.design: Forest Service Plan BC-201 fireman-lookout cabin, 19x30 ft, two rooms, with a 270-degree bank of windows in the back room

access.note: Rented to the public by reservation through Recreation.gov. It is a cabin, not a tower to climb.

visit.trail_note: Remote; much of the drive is on gravel Forest roads with no cell service. Reservations required.

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Shasta-Trinity National Forest

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps as a BC-201 fireman-lookout cabin. Sources disagree on whether it was used as a lookout.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Recreation.gov gives four people comfortably; the Forest Service page and the NHLR give six; one camping guide's fee line says up to 12. The story reports all three.

The NHLR describes an outdoor portable restroom and no running water; Recreation.gov and a camping guide describe an indoor flushing toilet with water for dishes or non-potable running water. The story reports both.
Recreation.gov and a camping guide say it was built as a wildfire lookout; the NHLR says BC-201 cabins were rarely used for actual lookout duty. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Design, 1934 build date and 2019 NHLR registration are well supported. Staffing and fire history were not found in the two searches and page reads, so the story says nothing about staffing; the record's staffing stays unknown. The record's access 'unknown' is set to public because the cabin is a reservable rental; a human may want to confirm the access wording. Name differs by source (NHLR 'Fireman-Lookout House', Forest Service and Recreation.gov 'Guard Station'). The record's built=1934 and nhlr_registered=2019 are correct; no corrections proposed. Capacity and plumbing conflicts are reported in the story, not resolved.
